summary: Kazuaki Komine studied at Waseda University (earning a doctorate in 1987). Working in Japanology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Tokushima University and the National Institute of Japanese Literature before serving as a professor at Rikkyo University (1995–2013).

Kazuaki Tanahashi, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology, studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as a scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center from 1977 to 1984 and became a fellow of the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. He served at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1982–1988) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013).

Working in history and archaeology, Kazuharu Mizuno studied at Nagoya University, Hokkaido University, and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc). Around 2009, he served as a professor in the Department of Geography at Kyoto University.

Kazuhiko Atsumi studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1948 to 1954 and worked in philosophy. He held positions at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1998–2008).

Active in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Kazuhiko Yoshida studied at Sophia, Kyoto, Cornell (under Jay Jasanoff), and Osaka universities. He taught at Nagoya City College for Women and served as professor at Kyoto University (~2000–2021).
Kazuhiro Furuta worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career included serving as editor and publisher at the Otani Academic Society in 1991 and as dean at Otani University in 1998.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kazuhiro Kawasaki completed his doctoral studies at Koyasan University around 2000–2005 and served as a researcher there around 2005.
Kazuhiro Yamamoto is a researcher in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Silpakorn University under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).

Kazumune Harada studied at Ryukoku and Koyasan universities under Kei Mikogami, Esho Mikogami, Hiroo Kashiwagi, and Makio Takemura. Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.
Kazunari Yamakawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his education at Sophia University and Aichi Gakuin University, where he undertook a master's program.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kazunobu Matsuda studied at Otani University. He held teaching posts at Otani University, Kyoto University, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University in 2009.

Kazuo Hyodo studied at Kyoto University and Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe. Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he served as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1984–2014) and directed the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute (~2005–2007).

Kazuo Kano studied at Kyoto University under Katsumi Mimaki and Hamburg University under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and David P. Jackson. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held professorships at Koyasan University and Komazawa University.

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Kazuo Matsumura studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1973–1977). He later held academic appointments at Tenri University (~1986–2004) and Wako University (~2004).

Kazuo Okabe studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, he served as an assistant professor (1973) and professor (1979–2006) at Komazawa University, also lecturing at Aichi Gakuin University in 1969.
Kazuo Oyamada studied at Tamagawa University from circa 1971 to 1975. A scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he held a post at Rissho University around 1991.
Kazutoshi Soma is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Meiji Yamada. He held a position as a lecturer at Ryukoku University in 1987.

Kazuyoshi Hotta, who works in Indology and Buddhist studies, completed doctoral studies and served as an administrator at the University of Tokyo in 2007. In 2015, he held a fixed-term assistant professor post at Otani University.

Kazuyoshi Kino studied at the University of Tokyo and worked in Buddhist studies. He founded Shinnyokai, served as president of Hosen Gakuen College in 1989, and became vice-president of Shogen Junior College in 1993.
